grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

topics.name: CONCEPT 3: MAINTENANCE OF THE ORGANISM
topics.description: Maintenance of the organism refers to a collection of biological processes and mechanisms, such as nutrition, respiration, circulation, excretion, and reproduction, that ensure an organism's survival and functionality.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 3.1 Nutrition in Man
sub_topics.description: Explores sources of food nutrients, classifies food types according to nutrient content, and examines the importance of essential nutrients for healthy growth and development in humans.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 3.2 Dietary needs of different persons
sub_topics.description: Focuses on designing and justifying appropriate diets tailored to persons with varying nutritional needs based on age, gender, body condition, and physical activity level.

competencies.description: Apply good eating practices for good health

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 3 3 Plant nutrients
sub_topics.description: Covers the identification and classification of essential plant macro-nutrients and micro-nutrients, as well as analyzing the effects of NPK fertilizers on crop growth.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 3.4. Nutritional deficiency diseases and disorders
sub_topics.description: Investigates the causes, symptoms, and treatments of various nutritional deficiency diseases and disorders in both human beings and plants.

competencies.description: Recommend appropriate food nutrients to address deficiency diseases and disorders in plants and human beings.

topics.name: CONCEPT 4: CONTINUITY OF LIFE
topics.description: The continuity of life refers to the principle that all living organisms are connected through shared evolutionary ancestry, supported by reproduction, transmission of genetic information, and evolution.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 4.1 Reproduction in living organisms
sub_topics.description: Investigates sexual and asexual modes of reproduction in living organisms, demonstrating propagation using seeds, spores, and vegetative parts, and comparing their characteristics.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of how living organisms reproduce.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 4.2: Reproduction and Development in Human Beings
sub_topics.description: Examines the structure and functions of male and female human reproductive systems, secondary sexual characteristics during puberty, and reproductive health hygiene practices.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of reproductive system in human beings

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 4.3. Reproduction in Viruses, Protozoa, bacteria and fungi
sub_topics.description: Outlines reproductive strategies across microorganisms—including viral replication, binary fission in protozoa/bacteria, and spore formation in fungi—and investigates fungal structure.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of reproduction in viruses, protozoa, bacteria and fungi

topics.name: CONCEPT 5.0: COORDINATION & RESPONSE
topics.description: Coordination and response in living organisms involve specific mechanisms for detecting and reacting to environmental stimuli. Two key types of responses are tropic responses in plants and taxic responses in motile organisms, which are critical for survival, growth and reproduction. In this concept, the sub-topics coordination and response in plants as well as coordination and response in animals will be covered.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 5.1- Coordination and response in plants
sub_topics.description: Plants, though lacking a nervous system, exhibit remarkable coordination and response mechanisms to adapt to their environment. These processes are vital for survival, growth, reproduction, and ecological balance. A knowledge of coordination and responses in plants can be applied to climate change mitigation, agriculture and food security, environmental interactions, ecosystem services and many more.
learning_objectives: Describe tropisms in plants
Investigate the effect of light and gravity on shoots and roots
Investigate the effect of water and chemicals on roots
Evaluate the importance of tropisms

competencies.description: Explore tropisms in plants and their relevance

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 5.2. Coordination and response in animal
sub_topics.description: Coordination and responses in animals are vital for survival and adaptation to dynamic environments. Taxic responses are critical as they enable animals to move directionally towards or away from a specific stimulus. The study of coordination and responses in animals particularly taxic responses provides valuable insights into animal behaviour, survival strategies and ecological roles.
learning_objectives: Describe taxic responses
Investigate taxic responses to light, chemicals and gravity
Evaluate the relevance of taxic responses to the organism
Apply the mechanism of taxic responses to eliminate pests and insects in homes
Differentiate tropic responses from taxic responses

competencies.description: Explore taxic responses in invertebrates and their relevance

topics.name: CONCEPT 6.0: ECOLOGICAL RELATIONSHIPS AND EVOLUTION
topics.description: Ecology is described as the study of the relationships between organisms and their environment. Ecological relationships refer to interactions between different species or organisms within an ecosystem while evolution refers to the scientifically supported theory that species of life have developed from a common ancestor. In this concept, learners will cover the following sub-topics: Ecosystems, Biotic and Abiotic Interactions, Waste Management as well as Soil Composition and Fertility.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 6.1 Ecosystem
sub_topics.description: An ecosystem refers to the community of organisms and their physical surrounding. Ecosystems can exist as terrestrial and aquatic. In every ecosystem there are biotic and abiotic components. The study of ecosystems is essential for understanding conservation and management, ecosystem services, human wellbeing and also climate change and environmental issues.
learning_objectives: Describe an ecosystem
Observe key features of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems in the local environment
Record key features in the ecosystems under study
Apply best practices to protect ecosystems
Construct models of different ecosystems

competencies.description: Explore features of ecosystems in the local environment.

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 6.2. Biotic and abiotic interactions
sub_topics.description: Biotic factors refer to the living components of an ecosystem and the interactions among them. These include predator-prey relationships, parasite-host dynamics and competition between individuals for limited resources such as food, mates and nesting sites. Abiotic factors on the other hand, are the non-living components of the environment.
learning_objectives: Distinguish biotic and abiotic factors in an ecosystem
Analyse the three kinds of relationships that exist in an ecosystem

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic: 6.3 Waste Management
sub_topics.description: Waste management refers to the collection, transportation, processing, recycling and disposal of waste materials to reduce the negative impact of waste on the environment, human health and aesthetics. Effective waste management results in conservation of resources, reduction of pollution and promotes sustainability.
learning_objectives: Analyse types of waste found in the environment
Evaluate the benefits of living in waste-free environment
Devise different ways of managing wastes in the local environment
Identify the challenges communities face which lead to accumulation of waste in the environment
Create waste-free zones in the environment
Reach out to communities in creating awareness on effective waste management practices

competencies.description: Manage waste in the local environment

sub_topics.name: Sub-topic 6.4 The soil - Composition and Fertility
sub_topics.description: Soil is a complex mixture of minerals, organic matter, water, air and living organisms. Soil fertility refers to the soil's ability to provide essential nutrients to plants in adequate amounts and proportions for optimal growth. Furthermore, soil composition and fertility are essential for optimising agricultural productivity, ensuring environmental sustainability, supporting ecosystem health, as well as achieving economic and food security benefits.
learning_objectives: Identify different soil components
Classify types of soil
Investigate features of fertile soil
Investigate causes of loss of soil fertility
Practice ways to improve and retain soil fertility
Compare crop yield in different types of soil
